title: How to come up with side project ideas: eight places to look for inspiration
summary: Ryan Hoover lists eight practical ways to find side project ideas, from reflecting on your own day-to-day to exploring emerging platforms, Product Hunt, GitHub and hackathons. He argues side projects make you a better builder and can grow into real businesses, as Product Hunt did.

principles.text: Side projects build skills and can become real businesses.
principles.quote: They can make you a better engineer, designer, marketer, or salesperson. Side projects can even turn into a business (Product Hunt started as a side project).

principles.text: Mine your own daily frustrations: log your day and spot what could be improved.
principles.quote: Often the best ideas come from one’s own experiences. Write a detailed diary of everything you do in a typical day and identify things that could be improved.

principles.text: Ask friends about their pain points to find problems worth solving.
principles.quote: Run through the same exercise above with your friends. Try to find frustrations or pain points that could be eliminated.

principles.text: New platforms create new opportunities, so dig into their APIs and docs early.
principles.quote: As platforms emerge and evolve, new opportunities arise.

principles.text: Take a feature of a favorite product and turn it into a standalone product.
principles.quote: Look at some of your favorite apps, sites, or products. Can you repurpose and improve upon one of its features as a standalone product?

principles.text: Great ideas are rarely forced in a brainstorm; stay exposed to the world and they find you.
principles.quote: It’s difficult to manufacture a truly great idea in a whiteboarding session. Sometimes they’re serendipitous, triggered by stories and changes in the world.
